records.text: Sarah Huckabee Sanders announced that Arkansas was launching Club America and would encourage students across the country to join.
records.speaker: Sarah Huckabee Sanders

appearances.snippet: We're so proud to have her and we're so proud of the incredible work that she is doing to help encourage students across the country to engage and join Club America, which we're launching here in Arkansas.

verification.notes: Arkansas Governor Sarah Huckabee Sanders and Erika Kirk announced a statewide partnership to bring Club America chapters to Arkansas high schools. Sanders' quoted remarks also praised the effort to engage students, matching the announcement in context.

sources.title: Governor Sanders and Turning Point USA's Erika Kirk Announce a Statewide Club America Partnership
sources.relevance: Official Arkansas governor release confirming the statewide Club America launch.

records.text: Charlie Kirk's mission was to have a Club America chapter at every high school across the country.
records.speaker: Erika Kirk

appearances.snippet: We're so grateful, and thank you for honoring Charlie Kirk. And Charlie and his legacy and his mission to have a Club America on every high school chapter across the country.

records.text: Owens read an unidentified social-media post promoting more than 500 high-school attendees at Erika Kirk’s TPUSA Club America tour stop at Nampa Christian School.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: So this person writes 500 plus outstanding high school student attendees at the Turning Point USA Club America Tour stop at Nampa Christian School this morning. ... Mrs. Erika Kirk delivered a powerful message to the generation of America. America first leaders, the future is bright.

records.text: Owens characterized Kirk’s Club America vision as voluntary grassroots growth and said she believed Erika’s mandated assemblies contradicted it.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I wrote back, hey, Andrew (Andrew Kolvet), Charlie (Charlie Kirk)'s vision never included forcing his ideas on students ever. He wanted to expand TPUSA organically. He wanted people to sign up for his events and clubs willfully. ... He believed in the free markets. He did not believe in forcing young kids to sit through a mandated assembly that they didn't want to attend so you could lie to donors about attendance numbers. ... Club America was envisioned by Charlie (Charlie Kirk) as a grassroots movement from willful students. Whatever the hell Erika (Erika Kirk) is doing is clearly. ... Clearly not that. And I do want to emphasize that because this feels like just a complete inversion of reality.

records.text: Kolvet described high-school assemblies as distinct from TPUSA’s regular chapter meetings.
records.speaker: Andrew Kolvet

appearances.snippet: Ah, concession. He's like gaslighting me about assembling high school. Did you actually never attend a school assembly in high school? ... These are distinct from our regular chapter meetings. I can't believe I have to explain.

records.text: Kirk said the high-school program was now called Club America and it had hired 80 new full-time people the previous week for that department.
records.speaker: Charlie Kirk

appearances.snippet: The high school program is now called Club America. We just hired 80 new full-time people last week. ... This is just full-time people just in the Club America department. What is their job? What do they do?

records.text: Kirk said Club America staff sourced leads from high-school students who wanted chapters, then met parents and administrators and guided students through the paperwork.
records.speaker: Charlie Kirk

appearances.snippet: Every day they are sourcing new leads of young high school kids that want to start Club America chapters. ... go there, meet with the parents, meet with the administration, fill out the paperwork. They're guiding the student through the process to get these chapters organized.

records.text: Kirk said success meant Club America chapters became a built-in school institution, like debate clubs, for students who loved the country, founding values and free markets.
records.speaker: Charlie Kirk

appearances.snippet: What we are trying to do is try to have full occupancy. occupation where it's not a question of, hey, do you have a Club America chapter? ... The question should be, are you going to your Club America chapter meeting? That's what success looks like. ... It's no longer like, hey, do you have one in your local school? It's why aren't you showing up to your local Club America chapter? ... You just kind of it's like built in. We want the Club America chapter to just be a built in perpetual motion machine that is there for students that love the country, love our founding values, love free markets and want to talk about.

records.text: Owens said forcing ideas on underage students was wrong whether done by the left or right, and supported clubs that interested students chose to join.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: You know, that is what I have always believed and what I still believe. Stop forcing ideas on underage kids. ... That's it. No. If you want to start a chapter or you want to start a club, you want to do this, great. ... If you want to then sell your ideas and kids are interested and they want to sign up, great. ... But this whole idea of mandating ideas, which is what this feels like to me, if you're mandating an idea, it's wrong. ... It was extremely wrong when the left was doing it. And it's wrong if the right is doing it too.

records.text: Owens accused TPUSA, Blake Neff and Andrew Kolvet of misrepresenting a required Nampa Christian school assembly as a successful voluntary Club America event attended by more than 500 high-school students.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Perfect example, case in point, Erika (Erika Kirk) does this event in Idaho. OK, that makes it sound like these high school students were willfully there and that they were high school students in general, 500 of them. ... None of that. That's also not true. And it just misrepresents the public as though Turning Point USA is expanding in some way. ... Minor students. I tell I just mentioned that it was actually a mandated assembly. And here come Blake Neff and Andrew Kolvet doing the absolute most on X, presenting to the public like this is a successful event that I'm lying when I countered that they were misrepresenting things.

records.text: The parent email author disputed TPUSA's '500 plus high school students' Club America description: middle-school students attended too, and these were students at a school-hours assembly, not 500-plus students who independently signed up for a Club America event.
records.speaker: Nampa Christian parent email author quoted in full (identity unverified)

appearances.snippet: This was not an event that was initiated or organized by the students. TPUSA publicly described the event as quote 500 plus high school students that were attending Club America. ... That was not an accurate description. The assembly included middle school students, so there were not 500 plus high school students in attendance. More importantly, These were not 500 plus students who independently chose or signed up to attend a Club America event. ... They were students attending a school assembly during regular school hours. Andrew (Andrew Kolvet), she's referring to Andrew Kolvet stated that only three students opted out.
